Perfume rating 3.85 out of 5 with 3,343 votes

God Is A Woman by Ariana Grande is a Oriental Floral fragrance for women. God Is A Woman was launched in 2021. The nose behind this fragrance is Jérôme Epinette. Top notes are Pear and Ambrette (Musk Mallow); middle notes are Orris and Turkish Rose; base notes are Madagascar Vanilla and Sandalwood.

I bought this as a dupe for Ellis Brooklyn Sweet. It's not exactly the same, but it's close enough for me to not spend the extra money on Sweet.

This is slightly juicier than Sweet and has a very synthetic top note that makes me crinkle my nose for the first few minutes. The dry down is much nicer though. Very sweet, juicy pear. Like sniffing one of those pear fruit cups as a child. I don't get any caramel as others have mentioned. Just clean, juicy pear.

It's an easy reach and I think it works for any season.

Updating my review to emphasize that the opening of this is pretty awful. I have to hold my breath until it settles down lol. After wearing a few days the dry down is really addictive.

This is one of my favorite fragrances as the note combo creates something unique - a boozy or better yet malty fragrance that is sweet and delicious. Although you could say there is similarity with "Born dreamer" due to the pear, but to my nose these are nothing alike as dreamer is a powdery, soft and enchanting fragrance - perfect for bedtime; while GIW is juicy and dark, like a hoppy/malty drink with is infused with dried fruit sweetness that can quench your thirst but still leave you wanting more. And I would say the fragrance is very linear, it is stronger the first 5-10min but then becomes lighter and lasts for 4-5 hours, sometimes even more. I'd say this can be worn year round. This fragrance is undeniably cute and sugary sweet, it is quite synthetic though. I knew it was geared more toward a younger audience, but I still wanted something light and cheerful to lift my mood – and in that sense, it delivered.

tieows 06/15/25 18:21

Now I like Ariana, not a superfan or anything but I think she's a great singer, and I saw a lot of hate for God is a Woman on social media, so when I saw a tester out in Chemist Warehouse I had to try it. I genuinely don't think anything could have prepared me for what that putrid liquid inside that cute little lavender bottle smelled like.
I have no idea what musk mallow is so I didn't really have any expectations other than the pickle claims from online, but oh my god I genuinely wished that all it smelled like was pickles. Immediately upon spraying it onto my hand, it shot to the back of my nose in a way that felt horrifying and attacking. My hand wasn't even close to my face but I violently flinched like someone had put smelling salts directly into my nostrils. I can only describe it smelling like someone had poured dehydrated, golden yellow piss into a stale week-old pint of beer and mixed the concoction with their unwashed scrotum. It was genuinely acrid, it smelled foamy and gritty, I'm struggling to articulate how violated I felt upon smelling this. If someone told me that this was used as a horse tranquilliser, I would unquestionably believe them.
Nothing changed as it dried down, the scent still stabbed itself into the very back of my nose and reminded me that this wasn't some cruel form of torture used by the CIA or something.
I have truly never felt this violated in my life, I don't know if this tester was just off, but I still get goosebumps thinking about that first waft that launched itself into my body and made my brain genuinely feel electrocuted.
I'm warning everyone to never challenge Ariana Grande with chemical warfare, if she's capable of producing something so punishing to the senses and selling it to the masses under the guise of pears and vanilla, I really do think she could make humanity go extinct with one atomiser spray.

Among all the Ariana scents that I have tried out, this is the one I liked the least. I knew I was playing with fire though, pear is a hard note for me.

Sparkleball22 03/30/25 10:29

Sweet sparkly pear grounded in a vanillic base with a quirky savory twist.
Another Ariana Grande perfume that is, like most of her line, bringing a surprising element to the mix while still being intriguing and fun. I’m starting to think I might explore this whole range. They really have personality.
I’ve been getting to know this perfume over the last few months, and my impression of it has changed quite a bit since my nose has become familiar with the pathway of first opening to dry down.
I suspect this perfume has something in the base that mimics sage, mate, or some other savory spice because it’s definitely in there, I can’t unsmell it now! I see that a few reviewers have picked up on that.
The fruity juicy pear and airy vanilla/iris is so pretty, and can float in the air around you. I don’t have a problem smelling this on myself, and it stays strong for hours. Good longevity, like 5-6 hours on me.

What I really like about this is that there are layers to it. My nose picks up on that, and it feels much more mature (not just teenager) than some people are giving it credit for!
That base of something more grounded and almost savory is what saves this perfume for me and takes it out of teen fleeting fruity mall body spray and puts it into a more sophisticated category, at least for me! Still really modern and uplifting. I think this range has really talented perfumers creating them!

Three similar fragrances, in order from juvenile to sophisticated:

Ariana Grande God is a Woman - juicy (almost candy), pear that is sweeter than the others because of vanilla, with slightly powdery/earthy musk

Ellis Brooklyn Sweet - sweet and powdery (because of marshmallow) pear (almost like "pear skin/peel", not "pear juice") with powdery almost soapy musk

Clean Reserve Radiant Nectar - fleeting sweet pear with an earthier musk that turns eternally, strongly clean girl musky on clothes (interestingly, the brief pear note makes this one's opening smell like boba, if you've ever cooked a brown sugar batch of it). But somehow, I wouldn't call it "soapy" the way Sweet can be 🤔, even though Radiant Nectar is definitely "clean girl musk". Just.. musky.

Do I need all three? No, but by now, AG GIAW is one of my gym scents (because it doesn't last long on me), Sweet is an easy warm weather reach with decent longevity on clothes, and CR RN... I LOVE the boba opening but I personally don't looove the base musk note.

kittenpawz 12/14/24 14:53

Jérôme Epinette is the man. He absolutely deserves the kind of recognition Quentin Bisch and Francis Kurkdjian get. Some create perfume. He creates memorabilia. And while I obviously cannot vouch for all of his creations, from what I've tried I've come to expect otherworldly and well put together fragrances whether they're for Byredo or, well, for Ariana Grande. They have a certain air of sophistication about them that people usually look for in MFK releases in which I personally find none at all. But Jérôme Epinette creates it rather effortlessly, and even if I cannot appreciate the scent itself due to individual notes I'm averse to, I won't dispute it being an intricate, well-blended perfume. And most importantly, while his style might be recognizable to a trained nose, his works don't really have something that screams the name of their creator in a very in-your-face manner as is often the case with Quentin Bisch (no offence though, I like quite a few of his fragrances too.)

So I'm happily adding GIAW to my small collection of Jérôme's creations and of AG fragrances as well. Most reviews of the fragrance don't fail to mention that this isn't the scent profile typically associated with the Ariana Grande brand, and mine won't be an exception. It's not the teenage girl Y2K body spray type of perfume. The synthetic/plasticky DNA you might be familiar with from sampling Ari or its flankers is gone, in its place this fragrance has an entry-level niche quality, courtesy of the perfumer who dare I say excels at niche. GIAW replicates the familiar molecule of BR540, Cloud and the like and takes it down a notch to an acceptable level. I had worn BR540 Extrait a few days before I blind bought this one and while Kurkdjian's Extrait was a scrubber because of the iodine smell as well as this very molecule, in Epinette's GIAW it's so smooth and inoffensive that it was love at first sniff, and I'm a very hard to please customer. Not to mention that the lack of any links to a medical intervention played its part, too.

The scent itself is without a doubt on the grownup territory, more young adult than adolescent as opposed to previous releases. Personally, I've always loved the happy-go-lucky, carefree & juvenile atmosphere they create, so people calling GIAW mature certainly wasn't swaying me in favor of purchasing it. But it is mature only by comparison: as much as Ariana Grande's early releases succeeded in supplying the demand of a modern bobby soxer, GIAW succeeds in becoming the next step in her fragrance journey. She doesn't listen to pop music as often and might not even know who Ariana Grande is or whose boyfriend the actress-turned-pop diva has got her eye set on now, and her own grownup date has the capacity to appreciate a fragrance that's more than just berry candy, even if she herself is not there yet to want to reach for the classics. No matter, because if she should ever grow out of Ariana Grande into Jean Patou, one day she'll take a sniff of GIAW again and think, "Damn, this was one beautiful fragrance!"

Beautiful is putting it lightly, but calling it a masterpiece still feels like an overstatement, so I'll settle on work of art. The pear opening is so deliciously gorgeous and so true to life here that I just want to gulp down the whole 100ml. In all seriousness, it smells exactly the way pear juice tastes; I checked recently. The first actual disappointment with this fragrance is that the intensity of the pear note fades down perhaps quickly. In the crook of the elbow it stays the way it starts the longest, but nonetheless throughout the day you'll still be catching whiffs off yourself that quietly whisper, "yes, this is the yummiest pear a fragrance could offer."
When orris root takes the stage, things get interesting. If the wide category of 'powdery' encompasses all things dusty, then the description is pretty accurate. You read it right: d-u-s-t-y, to me at least, and strangely, I like it. Whether you'll like it I have no idea, but the love to like, as well as like to dislike ratios suggest quite a few people do too or don't pick up enough of it not to like it. Although not literally, the strange combination of somewhat dusty orris and juicy fruit is indeed a breath of fresh air - what other fragrance offers exactly this, and what fragrance that offers it actually works?

The orris eventually settles into a softer, more cashmeran-like scent, and by the time I'm ready for bed I smell dewy, slightly powdery sweet pear. That's where GIAW's journey ends; it most certainly takes leave in the dead of the night, and by the time you wake up it's long gone, since, well, it's not a powerhouse. But need it be? I'm of the opinion that it does not, because the way things stand it has the qualities of a bedtime companion; cozy day, pity party or pillow talk situation. I've always found Ariana Grande perfumes acceptable in terms of performance, and I'll state it clearly that this is the worst performing one for me so far, but I can't really be mad. If it works it works.

My two cents regarding the name - look, I'm not a fan of either, I mean, I bet answering what you're wearing feels pretty awkward. But think of it as merely a marketing strategy: the brand uses the names of her most popular songs to appeal to the audience that likes them by creating a connection between the song and the perfume. If you could wear your favorite song - ah, maybe *you* wouldn't, however - it's a tempting offer to the target audience.

ShadowsofLight 10/05/24 19:03

Not a huge fan of the name of this, so I neglected to test it for a year or longer.

However, this is enjoyable and holds up as a fairly decent celebrity perfume. A.G fragrances typically are so far in my experience.

It opens with a tart fruity note, but not quite sour. I'm pleased that the pear here doesn't smell like canned cocktail fruit, as many pear containing fragrances do. It's kind of challenging though actually, because it has a some abrasiveness until it settles (after about 5 minutes). I prefer this over the cloying pear trending in modern perfumery though.

After this dries a while, the soft orris takes over and it begins to smell musky, though in a clean, clean way. Not in a Narciso Rodriguez manner (IYKYK), but in a more youthful way. I can understand why, because the target audience might be musk-shy. I've never thought of this before, but I'd recommend this to someone specifically looking for a "intro musk" fragrance, it's nice, friendly, and a musk that doesn't demand huge fortitude to pull off. It fact, I'd say this is quite crowd-pleasing, and an easy-reach.

It's PLUSHY in texture, and makes me sleepy. The vanillic drydown and soft sandalwood meld seamlessly. Some people are describing this as "vibrant" or "outgoing"...but no...not in my mind at all. I politely disagree, this is pillowy, relaxed...and makes me want my bed (in a good way). It's not sensual necessarily though, just pajama-y 😆😊🛏🌌


No, performance isn't stellar, but this also doesn't cost a mortgage payment, so I have no complaints.

**To me this is the only Ariana Grande perfume that I'd wear as most of them are either too coconut-y or too sweet and young for me personally. This was the first one in her line that I thought, "Woah! This is different and in the best way possible."

The wear : Wearing this, I have gotten compliments so the sillage is there. Most of those compliments have come from people at conversation distance or passing by. There's an absolutely gorgeous pear note 🍐 in this and a light floralness compliments that note nicely. I don't distinguish the vanilla or sandalwood but I can feel how this works with the rest of the notes to make the scent smell wonderful. Great date night and warm/sunny weather perfume!

Similar to: This is one of those few perfumes I can say remind me of another, very reminiscent of Burberry's Her EDT, and I think that's due to the juicy pear. It's not the same, don't get me wrong, Her EDT is more elevated, and lasts crazy long compared but there's a trace of that DNA in this. This would be one of the few celebrity perfumes that I think can be up there with the better perfumes, lasts long and doesn't disappoint!

Total rating: 4.5/5
Young but not youthful

After reading online that this might be a dupe for Liis Studied, a fragrance I love very much but cannot currently afford a full bottle of, I made a point of going to Ulta to test it. I sprayed on probably the last two-three sprays in the bottle, and wore it the rest of the day on my wrist. This opens with the crisp pear scent that is very similar to Studied, but unfortunately then moves into a warm, but somewhat sour base. There’s a weird unpleasant savory spice or tangy quality in this that is not at all in Studied, but does remind me of Eilish 1, another fragrance I do not like.

These notes in God is a Woman are very discordant to me and unpleasant. I also don’t detect any of the promised orris, a note I usually love.

Hard to tell the projection, but this has moderate wear time on me.

Overall, I would give this a 2/10, solely for the pear top note and decent lasting power.

I pretty much need a new bottle every year. Normally I wait till Christmas and get the gift set at Ulta with the body wash ornament, and the dopper bottle, and a 3.4 size big bottle. I adore how fresh and juicy this bottle looks when out of the included stand, it is gorgeous standing by itself. This smells to me like a big juicy pear, and that Ambrette makes it a bit more of a clean-girl/mature scent than other Pear scents in Ariana's line. The Madagascar Vanilla is very understated on the dry-down but mellows out the pear a lot, and this opens very jolly rancher candy and florally and dries down a bit more sensual than you'd excpect. I get tons of compliments wearing this, and I work in the food service industry so I'm always looking for perfumes that cover the smell of grease and fast-food, this does the trick. Its also the sandalwood that makes this more mature, but its a welcomed change to the opening notes. I adore pairing this with Poppy from Bath and Body works, or Carried Away. If you like this, you probably like Pear perfume.

tony5596 08/03/21 06:11

I've been eager to talk about this fragrance ever since i received it. For starters, I'm not too fond of the bottle. I appreciate the simplicity, but i feel like the cap should have at least been the same color as the base holder. When i first seen the notes, i was very intrigued, as i am a fan of Irris/Orris. Upon first spray, i get a blast of sweet Pear and Orris. It reminded me of a cross between Cloud and Thank U Next 2.0. because of the fruitiness.This fragrance already have some mixed reviews, so i was very skeptical at first. But this was a pleasant surprise, scent wise. As this settles, i get a slight woody accord. But that Pear & Orris is what i mainly get from this fragrance. No Turkish Rose or Vanilla. But Overall, the scent is pretty decent. I wasn't disappointed, but my expectations were barely met. Some have said this is a more mature scent from Ariana, and I'm going to have to totally disagree. This is just as fruity, if not, fruitier than her previous fragrances. Unfortunately, this fragrance lasted only 2 hours on my skin, and that's being generous. GIAW sits very close to the skin after 20 minutes of wear and begins to fade after an hour and a half. I feel like GIAW will make a perfect pairing scent with TUN 2.0. They seem like they'd compliment each other so well. I love that Ariana is going vegan with her brand, but if vegan means poor performing fragrances that remind me of her previous fragrances, then my days of collecting her fragrances will probably end with this one. Not trying to be negative because I'm a fan of Ariana, but as a fan, it's very important to be honest. I hope Ariana and Luxe Brands take heed to the criticism and use it as fuel to bring us something better next year.💜

I've tested this twice now in Ulta, and it's basically identical to Radiant Nectar by Clean and Sweet by Ellis Brookyln--a sweet, soft, marshmallow-y pear with a skin musk. I own both Radiant Nectar and Sweet and wear them frequently. I love the fragrance itself, but God Is A Woman is pretty weak, stays close to the skin, and doesn't last more than a couple hours--and that was with doing 4-5 sprays on my arm.

If you like the actual scent of this, just buy Radiant Nectar from Clean. Same fragrance, similar price point, but much better longevity. And if you already own Radiant Nectar or Ellis Brookyln Sweet, you do not need this.

I ADORE Cloud, R.E.M. and Thank U, Next so I was excited to get to the store and test this, but once I did, I realized I already have 2 perfumes that smell just like it already. So, it'll be a pass for me!

L.A.B33 08/09/21 11:12

I HATE this. Rarely do I find a fragrance that really falls into the "hate" category for me, but to me, this is a cacophony of notes that , individually, I can handle...but when placed all together? Ugh. Nope. Orris root is typically not a note I gravitate toward. It's too earthy, often bordering on dusty, to my nose. However, there have been some compositions (O Unknown! by IA) that I like it in. Ambrette (and amber) can sometimes smell like dirty skin/hair to my nose, but again, there are some compositions (Wanderlust Sublime by MK) where the amber/ambrette works and smells like "your skin, but better" and not dirty/animalic. Then there is the oh-so-trendy pear, which lightens up La Vie Est Belle, but here, combined with the vanilla, becomes too cloying and sickly sweet. So the combination all together is dusty, dirty, and sickenly sweet. It gives me the image of a child who has been outside all day eating various candies in the hot sun. I am 100%, sadly, not a fan.
